summary: Visible change: a message rendered in the browser before react-markdown has loaded shows skeleton lines instead of its raw Markdown source. AiChatProvider now loads react-markdown when it mounts; new preloadMarkdown() in glirastes/react. Server HTML is unchanged.
howTo: Nothing to do. While loading, [data-component="markdown"] contains div[data-element="markdown-skeleton"][data-state="loading"][aria-busy="true"] with up to 8 span[data-element="markdown-skeleton-line"] (estimated from the source) and a visually hidden text for screen readers (locale key markdownLoadingLabel, optional, English "Loading message…", German ships; not announced). Its size is inline, so it takes space with unstyled and in own layouts too; adjust it with --cm-markdown-skeleton-color, --cm-markdown-skeleton-line-height, --cm-markdown-skeleton-gap, --cm-markdown-skeleton-radius and --cm-markdown-skeleton-padding. The panel stylesheet adds a pulse, off under prefers-reduced-motion. react-markdown is now downloaded when AiChatProvider mounts, also while a floating chat is still closed, unless components.Markdown or components.MessageBubble is set; call preloadMarkdown() to start earlier (same promise on every call, never rejects, safe on the server). Tests that read the text of [data-component="markdown"] right after render now see the skeleton: wait for the rendered Markdown (findBy…/waitFor, or await preloadMarkdown() before rendering; React still suspends once on the first render). Server rendering (renderToString and streaming) and hydration are unchanged. For mention chips in a chat restored with session.load or createLocalSessionStore, set entityDeclarations; the streamed declarations are not stored.
